messages:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — presales sync with NovaHealth tomorrow 10am. They want a 4-week pilot (POC) and pushed hard on success criteria + regression gates. Need a compact eval plan we can show them.
Tori Li: Got it. What are the core flows they care about?
Maria Gomez: Clinical-note summarization + question-answer over chart data. Also a small reranking use for recommended follow-ups.
Sam Patel: Pricing flag: they asked whether to run hosted or Dedicated for the pilot. Ballpark for ~50k tokens/day on hosted?
James O'Neill: Also security Qs — they require KMS + VPC option and an initial SOC2 checklist. I can draft answers but need confirms on data retention and PHI handling.
Alex Kim: Good — let's scope: 1) success metrics (latency, quality, hallucination), 2) eval harness (golden dataset + holdout + automatic scoring + manual spot-checks), 3) rollout timeline and pricing option.
Tori Li: Proposed success criteria draft: p95 latency < 300ms on the targeted model; semantic F1 >= 0.80 on golden QA set; hallucination rate < 2% measured on random sample of 200 queries; availability 99.5% for the pilot window.
Maria Gomez: For the golden dataset I'm thinking 300 labeled items: 200 QA pairs across intents, 50 summarization seeds, 50 rerank cases. Split: seed 100 (for quick demo), holdout 200 for scoring.
Sam Patel: Hosted estimate: assuming gpt-like open model on our hosted infra, rough cost = ~ $0.018/token effective per 1k? (need final calc). Dedicated quote will be month-based; I'll get numbers and a simple TCO comparing them.
James O'Neill: Security: we can propose Private deployment on their GCP VPC + KMS. For SOC2 questions I'll mark data retention = 30 days by default, option to purge on request. Need product sign-off on PHI handling (redaction & consent).
Alex Kim: Eval harness specifics — minimal example to present:
```
- golden_seed.csv (100): labeled Q -> expected answer + intent tag
- holdout.csv (200): for automated scoring
- scoring config:
    - exact_match_threshold: 0.8
    - embedding_recall_at_5: 0.9
    - hallucination_flag_threshold: 0.02
    - manual_spotcheck_pct: 5%
```
Tori Li: For scoring, I'd prefer combined metric: 0.6*F1 + 0.4*embedding_recall, and require hallucination_rate < 0.02 as a hard gate. We should show a pass/fail and a continuous dashboard.
Maria Gomez: I'll seed the 100 quick demo examples today — focusing on high-value clinical intents. Also will add a short annotation guideline for labelers (how to mark partial credit, hallucinations).
Sam Patel: I'll produce two pricing scenarios by EOD: hosted pilot (pay-as-you-go) and 1-month Dedicated stub (reserve 1-2 GPUs). Will include estimated overage and burst costs.
James O'Neill: I'll attach the SOC2 answers + a short PHI handling note. sec-bot: uploaded /files/sec/novahealth-soc2-answers-v1.pdf :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: Task owners + timeline: Maria (golden seeds) by EOD, Tori (scoring rubric + dashboard mock) by tomorrow noon, Sam (pricing scenarios) by EOD, James (sec answers + data retention text) by EOD. I'll assemble and produce the one-pager for the call.
Tori Li: Quick Q: for regression detection — do we want a rolling baseline (last 7 days) or fixed baseline from the seed run?
Maria Gomez: Suggest fixed baseline from initial pilot run so we can detect drift vs the initial accepted performance. Rolling baseline can hide slow degradation.
James O'Neill: Agreed — fixed baseline for first month, then move to rolling with alert thresholds (5% relative drop on combined metric triggers review).
Sam Patel: Noted — pricing will include a line for eval harness compute (batch scoring) and an optional nightly rerun to detect regressions.
Alex Kim: Perfect. For the customer call I'll have the one-pager + a short demo using the seed 20 examples live. If anything slips, ping me in thread. :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: Uploaded seed draft to /files/pilot/nova-seeds-v1.csv.
sec-bot: file uploaded: /files/sec/novahealth-soc2-answers-v1.pdf
Tori Li: LGTM. See you on the prep call 9am.
Alex Kim: Thanks team — this looks ready. I'll send the invite and attach the one-pager once it's assembled.
